data.close_reason: Both artifact classes this story would clean up no longer exist, so there is nothing for the proposed close phase to do. (1) The held-out-twin convention was retired outright by 0b5d004f394; `git ls-files | grep -i 'heldout|held_out'` returns 0 tracked files, epic 6ed2-24e5 is closed, and rebar-implement now holds tests outside the worktree under `$(git rev-parse --git-path heldout)/` (SKILL.md:258-262) and restores them in Phase 4e (:286) — no twin module is ever produced. (2) All 5 seam-guard modules the story names are already deleted (590a32a175c, 303da730d5d, fcc171c16c0, b91f8f6830c, 8093c94e151), ADR 0058 now forbids creating new ones, and `seam-guard`/`seam_guard` appears nowhere in src, docs, or examples — so the deletion AC has no identifier to key on. The surviving `*_split.py` and `*_seam.py` modules are API-contract tests, not LOC guards. The one live residue this story surfaced — nothing enforces ADR 0058's no-hard-coded-ceiling rule — is owned by sibling f86e-b57b-008d-4652, which the operator rescoped to add a `loc-ceiling-pinning` antipattern to the code-review `tests` rubric. Closing obsolete rather than repointing avoids two tickets owning one change.
